faq.q: Do I need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2040?
faq.a: No, if you book a skippered charter with us. Our licensed skipper handles all navigation and safety. You just relax. For bareboat charters (where you drive), you need a valid Spanish PER or an ICC (International Certificate of Competence) endorsed for coastal waters.

faq.q: What is the PER licence and do I need it for Marbella?
faq.a: The PER (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo) is the Spanish recreational boat licence. It is required for bareboat charters on vessels over 6m or with engines over 40 kW. For skippered charters (our standard offering), you do not need a PER – the skipper holds it.

faq.q: Is an ICC accepted in Marbella for yacht charters?
faq.a: Yes, the International Certificate of Competence (ICC) is widely accepted in Spain for bareboat charters, provided it covers coastal waters and your home country issues it. Always carry your original ICC and passport. For skippered charters, no ICC is needed.

faq.q: What documents do I need to bring for a skippered charter?
faq.a: Just a valid passport or EU identity card for each passenger. No licence, no certificates. The skipper has all required qualifications. We recommend making a photocopy of your ID for the charter agreement.

faq.q: Can I charter a boat in Marbella without any boating experience?
faq.a: Absolutely. All our charters include a professional skipper who handles the boat. You can enjoy the coast from Cabopino to Estepona without touching the helm. It is the most popular way to explore the Costa del Sol.

faq.q: What are the 2040 updates for yacht charter licences in Spain?
faq.a: From 2040, Spain may implement EU-wide digital licence verification systems for bareboat charters. This means your PER or ICC could be checked electronically at the marina. For skippered charters, there is no change – the skipper remains responsible.

faq.q: Do children need a licence to be on a charter yacht?
faq.a: No. Children are passengers and do not need any licence. They must wear a life jacket when on deck (provided free). Our boats like the Lagoon 380 and Azimut 58 Flybridge are family-friendly with shaded areas.

faq.q: What happens if I charter a boat without a licence in Marbella?
faq.a: If you operate a boat without the required licence (e.g., bareboat without PER/ICC), you face fines up to €3,000 and potential seizure of the vessel. To avoid risk, always book a skippered charter – we handle all compliance.

data.body_html:
Planning a yacht charter in Marbella for 2040? The rules around licences are straightforward, but they have evolved. Whether you want to skipper yourself or relax with a professional, this guide covers everything you need to know. From the Spanish PER to the EU-wide digital checks, we break down the yacht charter license requirements Marbella 2040 so you can hit the water without stress.

Do You Need a Licence for a Skippered Charter?

No. If you book a skippered charter with us, you never need a licence. Our licensed skipper holds all required qualifications (PER or higher). You just bring your passport and enjoy the ride. All our boats – from the Astondoa 40 to the Mangusta 80 – depart from Puerto Banús with a skipper included. This is the most popular option for 99% of our guests.

Bareboat Charters: When a Licence Is Required

If you want to charter a boat without a skipper (bareboat), you need a valid Spanish PER (Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo) or an ICC endorsed for coastal waters. The PER allows you to operate vessels up to 12m and 12 pax. For larger yachts, you may need a higher qualification. We do not offer bareboat charters – all our trips include a skipper for safety and convenience.

What Is the Spanish PER Licence?

The PER is Spain's recreational boat licence. It requires theory and practical exams. It is valid for life once obtained. For EU residents, an ICC from your home country is usually accepted. For non-EU visitors, you can obtain a temporary PER or rely on skippered charters. Our fleet of 16 boats – including the Azimut 58 Flybridge and Ferretti 94 – all operate with licensed skippers.

2040 Updates: Digital Licence Checks and EU Harmonisation

From 2040, Spain may implement mandatory digital licence verification for all bareboat charters. This means your PER or ICC could be scanned at the marina office. For skippered charters, there is no change. We recommend carrying a printed copy of your licence if you plan to drive. For our guests, the skipper handles everything – no digital checks needed.

What Documents Do You Need for a Skippered Charter?

  • Valid passport or EU identity card (for each passenger)
  • No licence, no certificates, no experience required
  • We recommend a photocopy of your ID for the charter agreement
  • All safety equipment, insurance, and IVA (21%) included

Can You Charter a Yacht Without Any Boating Experience?

Yes. Our skippered charters are designed for complete beginners. You can relax, swim, and explore the coast from Cabopino to Estepona. The skipper handles navigation, anchoring, and safety. It is the easiest way to enjoy the Mediterranean. Popular routes include the Golden Mile, Cala del Faro, and Cala Cortés.
